news.title: SOS Foundation Signs MoU with BECS to Promote Education for Out-of-School Children in Islamabad
news.caption: Representatives of SOS Foundation and BECS at the signing of the MoU.
body: SOS Foundation has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Basic Education Community Schools (BECS), Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training, to strengthen access to education for out-of-school children living in the underserved communities and slum areas of Islamabad.
Through this collaboration, both organisations aim to establish educational facilities, promote literacy, and provide learning opportunities to children who lack access to formal education.
This partnership reflects a shared commitment to making education accessible to every child and building a brighter, more inclusive future through the Education for All initiative.

news.title: SOS Foundation Organises Literacy Walk on International Literacy Day
news.caption: Students, teachers, social workers and citizens during the Literacy Walk organised by SOS Foundation on International Literacy Day.
body: Islamabad, 8 September 2026: On International Literacy Day, SOS Foundation organised a Literacy Walk from Mr. Books, F-6 Markaz to the National Press Club, Islamabad, to highlight the urgent issue of 26 million out-of-school children in Pakistan.
Students, teachers, social workers, and citizens joined the walk to advocate for Article 25-A of the Constitution of Pakistan and UN Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG-4): Quality Education for All.
The participants called for collective action to raise awareness, inspire concrete steps, and ensure that every child's right to education is upheld.

gallery.alt: Children and an adult behind a banner, holding placards with literacy slogans.
Schoolboys in uniform hold a Walk for Literacy banner and placards.

news.title: SOS Foundation, ICCI and EduTransform Organise Teachers' Training Workshop on 21st Century Teaching Skills
news.caption: Participants, guests and organisers at the One-Day Teachers' Training Workshop on 21st Century Teaching Skills at ICCI, Islamabad.
body: Islamabad, 24 June 2026: SOS Foundation, in collaboration with the Islamabad Chamber of Commerce & Industry (ICCI) and EduTransform, organised a one-day teachers' training workshop on 21st Century Teaching Skills at ICCI, Islamabad.

Sardar Tahir Mehmood, President ICCI, was the Chief Guest at the event, while H.E. Naeem Khan, Pakistan's Ambassador to Rwanda, graced the occasion as Guest of Honor and interacted directly with the participants.
Dr. Abdus Salam, CEO SOS Foundation, welcomed the participants. Dr. Aneela Malik, CEO EduTransform, conducted an insightful and highly engaging training session.
Educators from across the twin cities attended the workshop in large numbers. The participants appreciated the initiative and described it as the need of the hour for Pakistan's education landscape.
President ICCI Sardar Tahir Mehmood acknowledged and appreciated the efforts of SOS Foundation in organizing this important initiative.

news.title: RWU and SOS Foundation Sign MoU to Strengthen Academic and Community Collaboration
news.caption: Representatives of RWU and CEO SOS Foundation sign the MoU.
body: Rawalpindi Women University (RWU) and SOS Foundation have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen cooperation in education, research, and community development.

The MoU was signed by representatives of both organisations in the presence of faculty members and officials. Under the agreement, the two institutions will work together on joint initiatives that create learning opportunities for students and contribute to the wider community.

Both sides expressed satisfaction over the agreement and said the partnership would open new avenues of collaboration. They agreed to turn the MoU into practical programmes and activities in the coming period

news.title: RWU Vice Chancellor Presents Appreciation Award to CEO SOS Foundation
news.caption: Vice Chancellor RWU presents an appreciation award to Dr. Abdus Salam, CEO SOS Foundation.
body: The Vice Chancellor of Rawalpindi Women University (RWU) presented an appreciation award to Dr. Abdus Salam, CEO of SOS Foundation, in recognition of the organisation's valuable services and its continued commitment to education and social development.

The award was presented during a visit of the SOS Foundation delegation to the university. The Vice Chancellor appreciated the Foundation's efforts and said that partnerships between academic institutions and organisations working for social welfare play an important role in building a better society.
Dr. Abdus Salam thanked the university administration for the recognition and reaffirmed the organisation's commitment to working closely with RWU. Faculty members were also present on the occasion.

news.title: RWU, SOS Foundation and NCHD Sign MoU to Promote Literacy
news.caption: Representatives of RWU, SOS Foundation and NCHD exchange the signed literacy MoU.
body: Rawalpindi Women University (RWU), SOS Foundation and the National Commission for Human Development (NCHD) have signed a tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to promote literacy and increase access to education.

Representatives of all three organisations signed the agreement and exchanged the signed documents. Under the MoU, the partners will join hands on literacy programmes, awareness activities, and joint initiatives aimed at reducing illiteracy and supporting learners across the community.

The participants said that collaboration between academia, civil society, and government institutions is essential for achieving meaningful progress in education. They expressed the hope that the partnership would bring positive and lasting results.

Two representatives sign the MoU at a table, with staff standing behind them.

stories.title: A Learning Space Where Every Child Belongs
stories.partners: In collaboration with Basic Education Community Schools (BECS), Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training
items: p

At ten years old, Ali had never sat in a classroom. In Sohan, on the edge of the federal capital, poverty, distance and the cost of books kept many children like him out of school, and each passing year made catching up harder.
p

Together with BECS, SOS Foundation helped create a learning space where these children could begin again. Children enrolled in accelerated learning programmes received complete educational kits. For Ali, as for many others, it was the first school bag and books he had ever owned. His teachers soon noticed a boy who arrived early, kept his books carefully wrapped and was eager to answer questions. Every child who returns to the classroom brings Pakistan closer to fulfilling Article 25-A of the Constitution and SDG 4.
q
"Now I have my own books. One day I want to become a teacher." (Ali, Sohan)

photo.alt: Two boys at an educational kit distribution; one holds a drawstring school bag.

stories.title: Healthcare at the Doorstep in Bari Imam
stories.partners: In collaboration with the National Health Services Academy (NHSA)
items: p

For Zubaida, a mother of four, her own health always came last, after school fees, rent and food for her children. Persistent fatigue and headaches had troubled her for months, but the cost of a doctor and the distance to the hospital kept her at home.
p

In collaboration with the National Health Services Academy, SOS Foundation organised a free medical camp that brought qualified doctors and volunteers into the heart of Bari Imam. Residents received free check-ups, screening, consultations and medicines, along with health and hygiene awareness sessions. Zubaida was examined for the first time in years, received medicines free of charge and was guided on follow-up care. She left with treatment, and with the knowledge she needed to look after her family's health.
q
"For the first time, someone asked about my health. I received care without worrying about the cost." (Zubaida, Bari Imam)

photo.alt: A health worker checks a woman's blood pressure at a medical camp.

stories.title: Learning to Read at Any Age: Adult Literacy in Rawalpindi
stories.partners: In collaboration with Rawalpindi Women University and the National Commission for Human Development (NCHD)
items: p

For most of her life, Shamim depended on others to read a medicine label, a child's school note or a bank form. As a girl she never had the chance to go to school, and every unread word reminded her of a door that had stayed closed.
p

In collaboration with Rawalpindi Women University and NCHD, SOS Foundation's Adult Literacy Programme gave Shamim a second chance. With patient facilitators and a supportive classroom, she learned to read, write and work with numbers. Today she reads her grandchildren's storybooks, signs her own name and checks her household accounts with confidence. When an adult learns to read, the whole family learns too.
q
"I used to put my thumbprint on everything. Now I write my own name." (Shamim, Rawalpindi)

photo.alt: Women sit together on the floor, writing on sheets of paper during an adult literacy session.

stories.title: Stitching a Path to Self-Reliance
items: p

In Muslim Colony, many women had talent and determination but no training, equipment or way to earn. Some were widows raising children alone, some depended on husbands with irregular daily-wage work, and others had skills they had only ever used at home. SOS Foundation launched stitching and embroidery classes for women and girls, and through a follow-up programme supported by our donors and volunteers, provided sewing machines to women in need.
p

What followed was a quiet transformation. Farha, a mother of three who once relied on others for everything, now stitches suits and school uniforms for her neighbours. Her earnings pay for her children's school supplies and help with the rent.
q
"Earlier, I waited for help with everything. Now I earn for myself." (Farha)
p
Nazia, widowed with two young children, now runs a tailoring service from a corner of her home and no longer depends on relatives each month.
q
"Now my children see that their mother works and earns on her own." (Nazia)
p

Sakina turned her gift for embroidery into orders for shawls and bridal suits, and she now teaches the skill to girls on her street. Other women have joined together to take bulk orders from local shops, so a single machine supports several families. One programme has grown into a circle of opportunity that keeps widening.
q
"What I received, I am now passing on to others." (Sakina)

photo.alt: A woman and a boy sit beside a new sewing machine.

stories.title: A Daily Meal, Served with Dignity
items: p

Rasheed, a construction labourer, works long, gruelling hours under Multan's scorching sun. His wages come and go and food prices keep rising, so a proper meal was often the first thing he gave up, so that his family back home could eat.
p

SOS Foundation's daily cooked food distribution brings hot, nutritious meals to Multan's labour community, prepared and served under safe food-handling and hygiene practices. Workers also learn about handwashing and food safety to protect themselves from illness. For Rasheed, a daily meal means the strength to work a full day, and more of his earnings sent home to his children. A simple plate of food, served with respect, tells every worker that their wellbeing matters.
q
"After a hard day's work, this meal gives me strength. It feels like someone cares about us." (Rasheed, Multan)

photo.alt: Labourers are served a cooked meal at an SOS Foundation meal distribution point in Multan.

stories.title: Clean Water for Mumtazabad
items: p

Nasreen, a mother of three, watched her children fall sick again and again from unsafe water. Like many families in Mumtazabad, she spent hours every day collecting water that was never truly safe to drink, and doctors' visits took money the family could not spare.
p

SOS Foundation installed a clean drinking water plant in Mumtazabad, giving the community reliable access to safe drinking water close to home. For Nasreen's family, the change came quickly: fewer stomach illnesses, fewer missed school days and precious hours saved every day. Safe water protects health, saves time and restores dignity, giving every child a healthier start in life.
q
"My children are not falling sick like before. Clean water has given us peace of mind." (Nasreen, Mumtazabad)

photo.alt: Officials hold a commemorative plaque outside the RO water filtration plant in Mumtazabad, Multan.

stories.title: Mobility with Dignity: Wheelchairs for PIMS Patients
stories.partners: In collaboration with Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS)
items: p

Abdul Rehman, a 62-year-old from a modest family in Islamabad, could barely walk after surgery. Every visit to the hospital for check-ups and tests meant his son had to hold him up through long corridors, because the hospital’s old wheelchairs were worn out and often already in use. For families already spending on medicines and travel, buying a wheelchair of their own was out of the question.
p

SOS Foundation, in collaboration with PIMS, donated 30 wheelchairs to the hospital. They replaced worn-out mobility aids and gave patients who cannot walk a safe, comfortable way to reach wards, labs and clinics. Abdul Rehman no longer has to wait or be supported on his feet. He reaches his appointments in comfort, and his family no longer has to struggle to carry him. A wheelchair may look like a simple piece of equipment, but for the patient who uses it, it restores independence, dignity and easier access to care.
q
“Now I can go for my treatment without being a burden on my family.” (Abdul Rehman, PIMS)

photo.alt: Rows of new wheelchairs lined up outside a hospital building.
